newsitem.title: USA: Texas Instruments aims to cut risk in market.
newsitem.headline: Texas Instruments aims to cut risk in market.

text.p: Texas Instruments said Thursday it is seeking to reduce its risk in the memory market and that it expects the semiconductor market for wireless communications to reach $9.5 billion in 2001.
The company said both are part of its strategy to provide value-added solutions for its customers and to gain a greater share of its revenues from differentiated products.
TI said it is "not yet satisfied" with its exposure to the volatility of the memory market and is "determined to reduce the effect of this market volatility on TI."

The company said its strategy also includes targeting high-growth markets and noted that the semiconductor market for wireless communications is expected to grow from $3.5 billion in 1996 to about $9.5 billion in 2001.
The company said it is focusing its digital signal processing solutions development on wireless communications, networking and mass storage devices.
"TI is leading the way in digital signal processing solutions that interface to office networks and will announce more products in this area in 1997 than ever before," the company said in a release.
Thomas Engibous, chief executive officer, told the Cowen & Co Electronics Conference that digital signal processing solutions will be a focal point of the TI's strategy generally.

He said the company plans to use its market leadership in digital signal processing to create a higher mix of value- added solutions that will differentiate TI's products and business profile over a sustained time, according to a release on his speech. He said this, in turn, will provide competitive advantage for TI's customers.
Engibous said TI's new TImeline Technology will enable the company to speed up the move in the industry to fully integrated "systems-on-a-chip."
These type of systems ultimately providing much higher performance at a lower cost of ownership, he said.

TI combines digital signal processing with mixed-signal chips (which means both digital and analog) to develop customized solutions for customers in the cellular telephone, modem and hard disk drive industries.
TI stock is down 1-1/8 to 53-7/8 in a day when the stocm market generally is down.
